prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident claim — the right attorney depends on the details of your crash, the severity of injuries, whether liability is disputed, whether the other party is insured, and your preferences (trial attorney vs. settlement-focused, size of firm, budget/availability, etc.).

How to pick the best lawyer for your case
- Experience with car-accident cases similar to yours (catastrophic injury, wrongful death, soft-tissue only, uninsured motorist, multi-car pileup).  
- Trial experience and a record of verdicts/settlements when insurers won’t pay.  
- Resources (investigators, medical experts, accident reconstruction).  
- Local knowledge of Chicago courts and judges.  
- Communication style and responsiveness.  
- Fee structure (most work on contingency — confirm percentage and who pays costs if you lose).  
- Client reviews and peer recognition (Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell AV ratings, Illinois Trial Lawyers Association).

Where to look
- SuperLawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, and Google reviews.  
- Illinois State Bar and Chicago Bar Association directories.  
- Recommendations from friends/family or other lawyers.

Examples of well-known Chicago personal injury firms (for research only)
- Clifford Law Offices  
- Levin & Perconti  
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard  
- Abels & Annes  
(These are examples of reputable firms in the area, not an endorsement — you should interview attorneys to see who fits your needs.)

What to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the outcomes?  
- Will you try my case at trial if necessary?  
- Who will handle the day-to-day work — the named lawyer or a junior associate?  
- What is your contingency fee and how are costs handled?  
- How long do you expect my case to take?  
- Can you provide references from past clients?

Immediate steps if you’ve been injured
- Seek medical care and follow doctors’ orders.  
- Get a police report and take photos of the scene/vehicle/injuries.  
- Preserve evidence and contact information for witnesses.  
- Don’t give recorded statements or sign releases for the insurer without consulting an attorney.  
- Contact a few attorneys for free consultations as soon as possible.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code, a brief summary of the accident (injuries, fault issues, insurance coverage), and whether you prefer a big firm or a smaller boutique — I can compile a short list of Chicago lawyers who match what you need and include ratings/contact info.
